summary: Documents version 2.0 of the IETF Administrative Support Activity, defining the roles of the IETF LLC Board, the IETF Executive Director, and the Internet Society in IETF administration. It replaced the structure established in 2005 as the IETF's needs changed.

eli5.summary: This explains the new rules for who runs the business side of the IETF, like a school's office staff, after the old setup changed.

questions: how is the ietf llc board chosen
subtitle: How the IETF's money, staff and legal home are organised under the IETF LLC and its Board.

tldr.problem: The IETF's needs evolved after the Administrative Support Activity (IASA) was created in 2005, and the original structure needed changes.
tldr.mechanism: IASA 2.0 creates the IETF Administration LLC, led by an Executive Director chosen by a small Board. The Board sets strategy and oversees; the Executive Director runs day-to-day work. The IAOC and IAD roles are eliminated.
tldr.outcome: The document obsoletes RFC 4071, RFC 4333 and RFC 7691 and sets Board composition, terms, funding rules and policies.

today: RFC 8711 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 101). It obsoletes RFC 4071, RFC 4333 and RFC 7691, and no later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: From IASA to IASA 2.0
sections.content:
The IETF Administrative Support Activity (IASA) was established in 2005. As the IETF's needs evolved, the administrative structure needed to change. IASA 2.0 moves administrative and fundraising work to the IETF Administration LLC (IETF LLC), a disregarded Limited Liability Company of the Internet Society (ISOC). The IETF Administrative Oversight Committee (IAOC) is eliminated and its oversight functions go to the IETF LLC Board.

The IETF LLC provides the corporate legal home for the IETF, the IAB and the IRTF, and financial support for the RFC Editor. This document obsoletes RFC 4071, RFC 4333 and RFC 7691.

It does not change the standards process run by the IESG and IAB, the appeals chain, the IRTF's technical work, or ISOC's membership in other organizations.
sections.eli5: The IETF got a new office team set up as its own small company, with a smaller group of supervisors replacing the old committee.

sections.title: Principles and Key Differences
sections.content:
The IAOC and IAD roles from RFC 4071 are eliminated. The Board of the IETF LLC is more focused on strategy and oversight, with the IETF Executive Director and their team in charge of day-to-day operations. The role formerly called "IETF Executive Director" in older documents is now "Managing Director, IETF Secretariat".

The IETF LLC is responsible for operations, finances, fundraising and compliance. It has no authority over the standards development activities of the IETF.

Its working principles are transparency, responsiveness to the community, diligence, unification, and careful handling of any transfer or dissolution. Whatever lacks a specific reason for confidentiality is expected to be public, and the Board keeps a public list of confidential items. Anyone may ask the Board for a formal review of a decision, and the IETF LLC typically responds within 90 days.
sections.eli5: The office team takes care of money and events but never decides how the Internet's rules are written. They are expected to share what they do.

sections.title: Executive Director and Board Roles
sections.content:
The IETF Executive Director is chosen by the Board and manages day-to-day operations, including hiring staff and contractors. The Executive Director develops and runs the annual budget, reports to the Board regularly, follows pre-approval guidelines for significant costs, and ensures staff follow policies such as a code of conduct.

The Board has fiduciary duties of loyalty, care and good faith. It sets broad strategic direction, adopts the annual budget, hires or terminates the Executive Director, approves governance changes and large agreements, and establishes an investment policy. It delegates day-to-day management to staff. Where this RFC and the LLC Agreement differ, the LLC Agreement and applicable law are authoritative.
sections.eli5: The director is like a principal running the school each day. The Board is like a small group that checks the big plans and the budget.

sections.title: Board Membership and Terms
sections.content:
There is a minimum of 5 directors, expandable to 6 or 7. They are 1 IETF Chair or delegate selected by the IESG, 1 appointed by the ISOC Board of Trustees, 3 selected by the NomCom and confirmed by the IESG, and up to 2 appointed by the Board itself and confirmed by the IESG. A Board-appointed director needs a two-thirds majority vote of directors in office.

Terms are three years, except that the IETF Chair slot has a two-year term. A director may serve no more than two consecutive terms and cannot serve a third until three years have passed. No more than three directors' terms should end in the same year.

NomCom-appointed and IESG-appointed directors may be removed with or without cause, with a vote of at least the number of directors less two, or through the recall process. Quorum is two-thirds of directors in office. Proxy and absentee voting are not permitted. The Board elects its own Chair annually, and the IETF, IAB and IRTF chairs and the ISOC Board chair are ineligible for that role.
sections.eli5: The supervisor group has five to seven people picked in different ways, each serving a few years, so no single group controls it.

sections.title: Funding and Policies
sections.content:
At the time of writing, the IETF LLC's income came from ISOC support, IETF meeting revenues, sponsorships and donations, either monetary or in-kind. The IETF LLC keeps its own bank account separate from ISOC and is expected to retain an independent auditor. The Executive Director sets meeting fees with Board approval.

Sponsorships and donations do not and must not convey special oversight or influence over the IETF's technical work. All funding is to be used solely for the IETF, IAB, IRTF and RFC Editor. The initial target operating reserve is the budgeted Net Loss for 2019 multiplied times three.

The Board is expected to maintain a Conflict of Interest policy, including that the IETF, ISOC Board, IAB or IRTF chair cannot chair the IETF LLC Board. It is also expected to maintain other policies such as a code of conduct, anti-harassment and data protection, and a compliance program reported to ISOC and the community annually.
sections.eli5: The money comes from donations, meeting fees and the Internet Society. Donors cannot buy a say in how the technical rules are written.

sections.title: Review, Change and Security
sections.content:
Any major change to the IASA 2.0 arrangements requires community consensus and deliberation and is to be reflected in a later Best Current Practice document. The IETF LLC, with the community, is to complete an assessment of IASA 2.0 after roughly three years of operation.

The document states that it introduces no security considerations for the Internet, and has no IANA considerations in the traditional sense.
sections.eli5: After about three years, everyone will check whether the new setup works well and fix what does not.
